newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends higher on central bank move.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends higher on central bank move.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed sharply higher against the dollar on Tuesday following the Central Bank's move to push down the U.S. unit, brokers said.
The rupee ended at 55.53 to the dollar after opening at 55.70 due to active selling of dollars.
"Banks sold dollars after the Central Bank pushed down the currency yesterday and today," said a foreign bank dealer.
The Central Bank set buying and selling prices at 55.3509 and 56.4691 respectively in the morning, 0.25 points lower than Monday when the authorities pushed down the dollar by 1.25 local cents.
Dealers said they expected the dollar to ease further during the week due to a lack of import covering.
"The dollar will probably come down to the Central Bank's buying level before firming again," said one.
Overnight call money closed at 14.5 percent, against 15 percent on Monday.
The market will be closed on Wednesday for a Buddhist holiday. Trading will resume on Thursday.
